children: Coca-Cola reported third-quarter 2026 net revenues of $13.38 billion, up 7% year over year, and diluted EPS of $0.93, also up 8%. Comparable EPS increased 11% to $0.91. The company raised its full-year outlook, now expecting at least 5% organic revenue growth and at least 11% comparable EPS growth.
Financial Highlights
Revenue:
Net operating revenues rose 7% to $13.38 billion. Organic revenues, a non-GAAP measure, increased 7%.
Gross profit:
Gross profit was $8.45 billion, up 10%; gross margin was 63.2%, compared with 61.5% a year earlier.
Operating income:
Operating income increased 12% to $4.47 billion. Comparable operating margin was 32.9%, versus 31.9% in the prior-year quarter.
Net income:
Net income attributable to Coca-Cola shareowners rose 8% to $4.01 billion.
Adjusted diluted EPS:
Comparable diluted EPS increased 11% to $0.91, compared with $0.82 in the prior-year quarter.
Business Highlights
Global unit case volume grew 5%. Sparkling soft drinks increased 5%, including 16% growth for Coca-Cola Zero Sugar; water, sports, coffee and tea grew 5% overall.
Volume was up 5% in Europe, Middle East and Africa, 6% in Latin America, even in North America and up 6% in Asia Pacific. Bottling Investments volume increased 8%.

The company gained value share in total nonalcoholic ready-to-drink beverages globally, with gains in Latin America, North America and Asia Pacific; it reported a share loss in Europe, Middle East and Africa.

Local campaigns marked Coca-Cola system anniversaries in the United States, Mexico and Nigeria. The company said Mexico and Nigeria activations contributed to quarterly volume growth, with Nigeria also recording value and volume share gains.

Across Europe, Coca-Cola and Sprite appeared at 60 music festivals in more than 20 markets, connecting brands with festivalgoers and livestream audiences. The company said the activations contributed to volume growth in the region.
